This Bail Application Having Come Up For Admission On 20.04.2023,
The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following:
 B.A. No. 1861 Of 2023
 2
 Order
Dated this the 20th day of April, 2023

The petitioner is the accused in Crime No.92 of 2023 of
Mannanthala Police Station.

Initially, crime was registered against the petitioner under Sections
294(b),
323, 324 and 341 of IPC.

2. The prosecution case is that, the accused, who was agitated by the act of de facto complainant for warning him for verbally abusing him, on 05.02.2023 with the intention to cause harm to the de facto complainant, wrongfully restrained him and assaulted him with a knife and thereby caused injuries to his left eye.
When the de facto complainant attempted to ran from away from the place of occurrence, the petitioner hit on his back.
The crime was registered in such circumstances.

Initially,
the petitioner was arrested and was released on bail 05.02.2023.
Thereafter, during the course of investigation B.A. NO. 1861 OF 2023 offence under Section 326 was incorporated.
In such circumstances, as the petitioner apprehended arrest, he submitted an application for anticipatory bail before the Court of Session, Thiruvananthapuram.
But the same was dismissed as per Annexure A3 on the ground that the same is not maintainable.
This anticipatory bail is submitted in such circumstances.

sentences.text: Heard Sri. Navaneeth N. Nath, learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner and Sri.C.N.Prabhakran, the learned Public Prosecutor.

4. Learned Counsel for the petitioner places reliance on a decision rendered by this Court in B.A.
No.8129/2022, wherein it was observed by this Court that, in a case where a accused is initially released on bail, on the ground that the offences involved are bailable in nature, and his arrest is required to be made consequent to the incorporation of non-bailable offences, it shall be B.A. NO.
1861 OF 2023 open for him to invoke the remedy of anticipatory bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.
It is pointed out that the aforesaid decision was followed by another bench of this Court in the decision reported in Nijam and another vs. State of Kerala; 2023 (1) KLJ 476 .

entities.text: Nijam and another vs. State of Kerala; 2023 (1) KLJ 476
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In such circumstances, it is pointed out that the petitioner is entitled to invoke the said remedy in the facts and circumstances of the case and he is to be granted anticipatory bail.
5.
On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor would oppose the aforesaid application by pointing out that there are serious allegation against the petitioner.
The recovery of the weapon is to be effected and therefore, his interrogation is necessary.
6. After considering all the relevant aspects, I find some force in the contention put forward by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

As regards B.A. NO. 1861 OF 2023 the maintainability of the anticipatory bail application, the said issue is already decided by this Court in BA No.8929/2022,
wherein it was held that it is maintainable.
When coming to the merits of the case, it is evident from the records that, initially the petitioner was released on bail.
7. No criminal antecedents of the petitioner is brought into notice of the Court.
Since the petitioner is already arrested and released on bail, I am of the view that, an opportunity can be granted to the petitioner to co-operate with the investigation.
Therefore, this application is disposed of directing the petitioner to surrender before the investigating officer.

Accordingly, this application is disposed of with the following directions:
i) The petitioner shall surrender before the Investigation officer for the purpose of ensuring his co-operation, within a period of two weeks from the B.A. NO. 1861 OF 2023 date of the order, for subjecting himself for interrogation;
ii) Upon such surrender and after interrogation, if any, the petitioner shall be produced by the investigation officer, before the Judicial First Class Magistrate having jurisdiction, on the very same day of surrender itself, to enable the petitioner to seek bail;
iii) The Judicial First Class Magistrate, upon production of the accused and filing of application for bail, may consider the bail application in accordance with law, and if possible, dispose of the same , on the very same day of filing of the said application,
subject to such conditions, as deem fit.
